text:
Maya: Quick one — Kotlin client streaming seems to cut out after ~1k tokens intermittently. Using OkHttp (HTTP/1 chunked) + our Jackson SDK. No exception, call just completes. Anyone seen this?

Jon: first check timeouts and whether the Source/ResponseBody is being closed early. Also LB idle timeouts can silently drop connections. What are your OkHttp settings?

Maya: default OkHttpBuilder. readTimeout was 10s. I tried setting readTimeout(0) once and it behaved better but flaky. Using try-with-resources to manage the response.

Eugene: a couple concrete tips: 1) For long-lived streaming set readTimeout(0) so OkHttp won't trigger a read timeout. 2) For HTTP/2 you can use pingInterval to keep the connection alive. 3) Make sure the app doesn't close the stream early. Example: 

```
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
  .pingInterval(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 64; maxRequestsPerHost = 16 })
  .build()
```

Eugene: also simulate a server that sends periodic tiny chunks so you can reproduce LB behavior locally.

Maya: is pingInterval useful for HTTP/1 chunked streams or only http2/ws? We are not using websockets.

Jon: pingInterval mostly helps HTTP/2. For HTTP/1 chunked, if infra drops idle TCP you need either infra keepalive or the server to emit heartbeat chunks. Some LBs have 60s idle timeouts by default.

Li: unrelated note — watch out for shading collisions. I pulled a transitive gson in and started seeing NoSuchMethodError / serialization oddities; our SDK expects Jackson.

Maya: i do have a transitive gson from a third-party lib.

Li: fix options: exclude gson transitively (preferred) or relocate it when building a fat jar. Example exclusions: 

Gradle exclusion:
```
implementation('com.vendor:thing:1.2.3') {
  exclude group: 'com.google.code.gson', module: 'gson'
}
```

Shadow relocation if you must keep it:
```
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.google.gson', 'com.redwood.shaded.gson'
}
```

Li: also run `./gradlew dependencies` or `mvn dependency:tree` to find duplicate JSON libs.

Maya: i'm getting ClassNotFound: okhttp3.internal.platform.AndroidPlatform in JVM integration tests. Any pointers?

Jon: that indicates an Android okhttp artifact made its way into the classpath. Force the JVM okhttp artifact/version in your test/runtime libs. Example force in Gradle: 

```
dependencies {
  implementation 'com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp:4.10.0'
}
configurations.all {
  resolutionStrategy.force 'com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp:4.10.0'
}
```

Eugene: and if you see Jackson UnrecognizedPropertyException, set the mapper to ignore unknowns (our SDK already sets this): 
```
objectMapper.configure(DeserializationFeature.FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES, false)
```

Maya: streaming parser question: i'm using Jackson's streaming parser to parse NDJSON from the same HTTP body. Sometimes parser fails on partial tokens when the server flushes mid-object. How to handle partial frames?

Eugene: best approach depends on framing: if server sends NDJSON (newline-delimited), read the body by lines and feed each complete line to the parser. If server doesn't frame objects, you need a framing protocol (length-prefixed) or rely on Content-Length per message. With InputStream parser: 

```
val parser = JsonFactory().createParser(inputStream)
while (!parser.isClosed()) {
  val token = parser.nextToken() ?: break
  // handle tokens, buffer until full object processed
}
```

Eugene: but if objects can be cut across flushes, line-buffering or application-level buffering is safer.

Maya: good call. i will: 1) exclude gson transitively, 2) set readTimeout=0 and avoid closing the stream prematurely, 3) add line-buffering for NDJSON parsing, 4) add an integration test that streams a very long payload and simulates slow chunks / LB drop.

Jon: re: tests — write a small Jetty/Netty test server that writes 5k tokens over ~30s with small pauses. That reproduced several edge cases for us.

Li: and double-check proguard/R8 rules on Android; shading + minification can remove reflective Jackson constructors. Add keep rules if you bundle.

Maya: thanks everyone, plan sounds solid. Will coordinate with infra about LB idle and devops-bot before modifying client timeouts. :rocket: 

devops-bot: deploy-checklist: note — if you change timeouts or keepalive behavior, coordinate with infra to avoid causing connection churn or unexpected resource usage.
